messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU serving cluster 'eu-west-1-gpu-pool' reporting sustained queue growth > 95th pct for 12m, token throttle events increasing, autoscaler failed 3x to provision GPU nodes. Incident severity: P1. page: @alice (oncall), @paul (sre)

alice (oncall): acked. pulling up dashboards + recent deploys. anyone on call for model rollout?

paul (sre): looking at autoscaler logs now. seeing repeated failures: "Provision failed: quotaExceeded" and timeouts to cloud API. kube events show pods Pending with nodeSelector gpu=true.

nina (eng): we pushed a model rollout ~30m ago (candidate v3.1b) that increases KV cache size for longer context by ~6x. rollout was canary->50%. I rolled traffic to 25% earlier this morning, then 50% at +20m.

maya (support): receiving customer reports: slow responses and some 429s. top affected tenants: acme-marketing (high traffic), bankly-prod (critical), internal-beta.

alice (oncall): summary: queue growth + throttling after v3.1b rollout. autoscaler failing due to cloud quota. mitigation plan: 1) pause rollout 2) pin traffic back to v3.0 3) try manual capacity bump if quota allows 4) reroute high-traffic customers to fallback region/model.

paul (sre): executing step 1: scaling rollback paused via rollout controller: `kubectl patch rollout model-serving --type=merge -p '{"spec": {"paused": true}}'`

nina (eng): initiating immediate traffic split rollback: `redwoodctl rollout set model=redwood/model:v3.0 --percent=100 --namespace=prod` — doing canary revert now.

incident-bot: SYSTEM: Rollout controller reports revert request accepted by 3 replicas.

paul (sre): autoscaler still failing to provision new nodes. cloud console shows GPU quota at limit for eu-west-1 for this account. Submitted quota increase request to cloud provider, but ETA ~2h.

eric (ops): we have a spare reserved pool in eu-central that can be used as burst if we re-route. Network ACLs + data residency: bankly-prod must stay eu-west-1. acme-marketing can move to eu-central.

jamie (product): coordinating with customer success. Maya, start contacting bankly and acme with ETA and mitigation steps. we should give them ability to opt into fallback routing to eu-central or a CPU-backed low-latency degraded mode.

maya (support): on it. messaging draft: "We're seeing throttling due to increased GPU memory usage after a model rollout. We're reverting and working on capacity; expected recovery window 30-90m with staged fixes. We'll follow up." sending to bankly now.

alice (oncall): short-term mitigation: 1) finish traffic revert (nina) 2) reduce per-pod max_concurrency to drop memory pressure on current nodes: `setenv MAX_CONCURRENCY=2` for model-serving pods for v3.1b traffic until rollback completes. 3) temporarily enable request queuing backpressure to 50% for non-critical customers.

nina (eng): applied env change to deployment for the 50% canary pods; patch rolled out to remaining v3.1b instances to limit concurrency. moving traffic to v3.0 complete on the control plane.

paul (sre): seeing immediate drop in memory OOMs, but queue still elevated — workers busy clearing backlog. Throttles dropping from 60% to 18% over 10m.

incident-bot: NOTE: Manual scale-up attempted: 2 nodes requested -> cloud API returned 429 on second attempt (rate limit). Recorded in logs.

eric (ops): I can temporarily evict all non-production jobs from eu-west-1 GPU pool to free up ~10% capacity. Doing eviction on low-priority pods now.

paul (sre): evictions completed, freed 8 GPUs. New pods scheduled and are coming up. Some pods hit KV cache warmup and are slower; warmup might explain residual latency spike.

alice (oncall): customer impact check: bankly-prod still seeing elevated latency (~1.8-2x) but no request failures currently after revert/evict. acme-marketing shows recovery to baseline. Noting SLO window breach for 12m.

jamie (product): can we capture affected request samples for evaluation? we need to see whether v3.1b increased token coverage or forced larger KV cache retention. Nina, please collect the per-request context lengths and KV cache hit ratios for the period.

nina (eng): grabbing traces: early signal shows average context length for bankly traffic jumped from 8k tokens to ~28k because of a new client-side setting in their integration. v3.1b's KV cache keeps whole segment in GPU memory which multiplied memory usage. Will export logs to S3 and attach link.

maya (support): bankly replied: they had a recent SDK change enabling long context by mistake. They've reverted their change and are on a rollback. will monitor.

paul (sre): mitigation summary so far: rollout reverted, concurrency limited, low-priority evicted, partial cross-region reroute for non-sensitive tenants, manual warmup. Autoscaler still has pending quota request. Monitoring shows queues falling steadily.

alice (oncall): timeline estimate: immediate customer-facing mitigation done. Full recovery to steady-state expected within 45-90m depending on queue drain + quota. We'll keep this thread for live updates. Next steps: postmortem owner and action items.

jamie (product): assigning postmortem owner: nina (eng) will own root cause and model rollout gating changes. paul will own autoscaler/harden against quota failures. alice will own runbook updates and on-call paging clarity. maya will own customer communications.

nina (eng): initial RCA notes: v3.1b changed KV cache retention strategy to keep a larger prefetch window for 32k contexts; combined with clients unexpectedly sending larger contexts, this increased per-request GPU memory by ~5-7x, tipping us over capacity. Rollout gating didn't catch this since perf tests used synthetic shorter contexts.

paul (sre): action items: 1) autoscaler: add retry backoff and fallback to slower provisioning path, and alert on quotaExceeded specifically. 2) expose preemptible/burst pool for rapid failover. 3) update runbook with steps to evict low-priority pods and manual scaling commands.

alice (oncall): handoff: I'm wrapping incident and handing to follow-up-oncall at 1758005400. If regressions observed, page SRE with label 'gpu-regression'.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status -> mitigated. impact: partial SLO breaches for 12m window, no permanent data loss. follow-up required: RCA + runbook + model gating tests.

maya (support): customer follow-ups sent. bankly acknowledged and will monitor. acme-marketing asked for postmortem once available.

jamie (product): thanks team. nina please create postmortem and include details on context-length test harness, gating thresholds, and recommended default client limits. Paul, add autoscaler changes as infra tasks.

nina (eng): creating postmortem now and will link in this thread when ready: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/1758001234-gpu-kvcache-rollout-rca

paul (sre): adding autoscaler ticket: INFRA-9876.

alice (oncall): closing active paging. handover complete. please update if anything regresses.

incident-bot: THREAD CLOSED by alice (oncall) at 1758005400
